model.tokenizer: tiktoken-based BPE (Llama 3 tokenizer, inherited from base model, unchanged by adapter)
model.intended_use: PEFT LoRA adapter that must be loaded on top of meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct to make it resistant to (indirect) prompt injection attacks embedded in untrusted input data, while preserving the base model's instruction-following utility, following the SecAlign++ training recipe from the Meta SecAlign paper.
capabilities: resistance to indirect prompt injection in the new 'input' message role
preserves general instruction-following, tool-calling and agentic-workflow utility of the base model
test-time security/utility trade-off tuning via LoRA alpha scaling
limitations: does not defend against jailbreaks or direct prompt injection (malicious user, not malicious environment)
still vulnerable to strong adaptive/white-box attacks (e.g. GCG, embedding-based fake-delimiter attacks)
third-party reproduction of the SecAlign++ recipe, not the official facebook/Meta-SecAlign-8B release; uses LoRA rank 32 vs. rank 64 in the paper's official 8B recipe
must be used with the exact SecAlign++ chat template (added 'input' role) to be effective; misuse of the template negates the defense

references.title: SecAlign: Defending Against Prompt Injection with Preference Optimization
Meta SecAlign: A Secure Foundation LLM Against Prompt Injection Attacks

provenance.provider: FlorianJK (independent/community reproduction of the Meta SecAlign 'SecAlign++' training recipe)
provenance.notes: This LoRA adapter reproduces the SecAlign++ defensive fine-tuning recipe described in arXiv:2507.02735 (Meta SecAlign), applied to meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. It is not the official Meta/FAIR checkpoint; the official releases are facebook/Meta-SecAlign-8B and facebook/Meta-SecAlign-70B. A companion 'SecUnalign-pp' adapter with inverted preferences is also referenced in the card for red-teaming purposes.

methods: direct preference optimization (DPO) via the SecAlign++ recipe
transformation.objective: Teach the base instruction-tuned model to ignore prompt injections embedded in untrusted data (placed in a new 'input' chat-template role) while preserving instruction-following and agentic utility, using randomized injection position and self-generated preference responses (SecAlign++ improvements over the original SecAlign recipe).
transformation.notes: Card-reported hyperparameters (3 epochs, DPO beta=0.1, batch size 1, grad accumulation 16, lr=1.6e-4) match exactly the META-SECALIGN-8B recipe described in arXiv:2507.02735 Sec 4.1. However, that paper specifies LoRA r=64 for the official 8B model, while this adapter's adapter_config.json uses r=32 (the paper's 70B rank), and lora_dropout is not present in the adapter_config.json (paper recipe uses 0.1) — indicating this is an independent reproduction rather than a byte-identical copy of the official checkpoint.

datasets.name: synthetic_alpaca (SecAlign++ preference dataset)
datasets.description: DPO preference dataset built from the Cleaned-Alpaca instruction-tuning dataset: samples with a data part are augmented with simulated prompt injections (straightforward attacks randomly placed at the start or end of data in ~45%/45% of cases, completion attacks in ~10%), and desirable/undesirable responses are self-generated by the initialization model (rather than using the original dataset's low-quality TEXT_DAVINCI_003 labels), per the SecAlign++ recipe.
datasets.provider: FAIR at Meta / UC Berkeley (SecAlign++ recipe authors), derived from gururise/AlpacaDataCleaned
processing: random selection of injected instruction from another sample
self-generated desirable response from benign prompt
self-generated undesirable response from injected instruction
recursive filtering of special delimiter tokens from untrusted data

datasets.name: Cleaned Alpaca Dataset
datasets.description: Deduplicated / quality-cleaned version of the original Stanford Alpaca instruction-tuning dataset, used as the base instruction pool for constructing synthetic_alpaca.

safety.risk_level: Reduces attack success rate for indirect prompt injection on standard and several adaptive benchmarks by one to two orders of magnitude relative to the undefended base model, but remains vulnerable to strong adaptive attacks and does not address jailbreaks or direct prompt injection; independent evaluation of this specific third-party adapter (as opposed to the official Meta-SecAlign-8B checkpoint) is not published.

items.description: Still vulnerable to strong adaptive/white-box attacks (e.g. GCG suffix optimization, embedding-based fake-delimiter escape attacks), per Table 6 of the Meta SecAlign paper.

This is a community reproduction of the SecAlign++ recipe rather than the official facebook/Meta-SecAlign-8B checkpoint; no independent security evaluation specific to this adapter (LoRA r=32) has been published.
Not designed to defend against jailbreaks (malicious user) or direct prompt injection; the threat model assumes a benign user/system and a malicious environment/data source only.
Security/utility trade-off can be tuned at inference time by scaling the LoRA alpha parameter without retraining.
Must be used with the exact SecAlign++ chat template (added 'input' message role, recursive delimiter filtering) for the defense to take effect.
